BookStatus.description:
Where a book is in the download pipeline.

A `StrEnum` rather than a plain `Enum` so a member *is* the text stored in the
`status` column: the database keeps the values it already holds, no migration
has to rewrite a row, and a comparison against a plain string still works.

`DOWNLOADING` exists so a scheduler tick starting while a download is running
cannot pick the same row, and `FAILED` is terminal - without it a book that
could never succeed was re-licensed, re-downloaded and re-failed on every run.

`UNAVAILABLE` is deliberately **not** terminal. A Plus title the customer added
while it was included stays in the library after Audible withdraws it but cannot
be licensed, and Audible does bring such titles back: 16 of a 306-title library
were withdrawn when this was measured (2026-09-09). Those books leave the download
queue so they stop costing a licence request every run, and `update_books` returns
them to `waiting_download` as soon as a sync sees them consumable again.
BookStatus.title: BookStatus

LoginOut.description:
A login in flight or finished. `status` is `pending` until the user has done their
part, then `confirmed` with the `account`, or `expired` (start again), `failed`
with the `error`, or `cancelled` (`DELETE /api/accounts/login/{login_id}`). The
`code` method carries `code` and `verification_url`; the `browser` method carries
`url`.
LoginOut.title: LoginOut

LoginStart.description:
Start signing in to a marketplace. The account the login will produce is described
here, since with the default `code` method nothing else is posted: `name` and
`monitor_existing` (whether the library the account already holds is queued for
download or inserted unmonitored so the user picks) for a new account, or
`account_id` to give an existing account the new credentials instead, keeping its
library - the way back when a registration stops working - with
`deregister_previous` removing its old device from Amazon first, best effort. Without
an `account_id`, a login an account already holds (the same customer and marketplace)
is treated the same way, and `name` and `monitor_existing` are not used.

`method` is `code` (show a code, the user enters it at Amazon on any device, the
service polls until confirmed) or `browser` (the user signs in at `url` in a browser
and posts the "page not found" address it lands on to step two).
LoginStart.title: LoginStart

QueueOut.description:

the queue as it stands now. `total` is how many are planned before any refusals
(a refused licence uses no slot, so a run can take on more), `waiting` how many
wait in those accounts in all, and `max_download` the per-account cut (None:
everything waiting). See `library.next_run_queue` for why it is a plan.
QueueOut.title: QueueOut

SettingsUpdate.description:
A partial update: only the fields sent are changed.

Every field is optional and defaults to "not sent", which is distinct from `null`:
`{"max_download": null}` clears the limit, omitting it leaves it alone. Unknown
fields are rejected rather than ignored, so a typo cannot pass silently.

`null` is only accepted for the three settings that can be unset (`max_download`,
`max_consecutive_failures`, `webhook_url`). Anywhere else it would be stored as
an empty value no later read could parse, locking the API out of its own settings.
SettingsUpdate.title: SettingsUpdate

SignIn.description: `POST /api/auth/login`. `remember` makes the session cookie outlive the browser.
SignIn.title: SignIn

SkipReason.description: Why a bulk action left a book alone; the UI words it.

SyncOutcome.description:
How one pipeline run ended.

A `StrEnum` for the same reason as `BookStatus`: a member *is* the text stored in
the `outcome` column, so a comparison against a plain string still works and no
row has to be rewritten to change the Python side.

`RUNNING` is written when the run starts and replaced when it ends, so a row still
`RUNNING` with no `finished_at` is a run that died half way - the thing the
library table could never tell apart from a run that simply found nothing.

`PARTIAL` means the sync completed but the downloads did not all succeed. It counts
as a cursor for the next run, because the library really was read; which books
failed is the `library` state machine's business, not the run's.

`CANCELLED` is a run somebody stopped. A cancel is only honoured once the library
sync has completed - the sync is seconds, the downloads are the hours - so a
cancelled run has always read the library through and counts as a cursor too. The
book it was on is handed back to the queue with its attempt count untouched.

`ABORTED` is a run that stopped itself: `max_consecutive_failures` books in a row
were refused a licence or failed, which means something is wrong with the account
or with Audible rather than with the books, and walking the rest of the queue would
only repeat it. Like `CANCELLED` it comes after the sync, so it is a cursor too;
the reason is in `error`.
SyncOutcome.title: SyncOutcome

SyncStart.description: What `POST /api/sync` may be sent; the body itself is optional.
SyncStart.title: SyncStart

WebhookTest.title: WebhookTest

schema.title: Response List Accounts Api Accounts Get

post.description:
Start signing in to a marketplace.

With the default `code` method the answer carries the `code` to enter at
`verification_url`, on any device; the service polls Amazon and the login turns
`confirmed` (with the account) on `GET /api/accounts/login/{login_id}` once the
user has entered it. With `browser`, open `url`, sign in, and post the "page not
found" address to `POST /api/accounts/login/{login_id}`. 422 for an unknown
marketplace or one that is not `account_id`'s, 404 for an unknown `account_id`,
502 when Amazon will not issue a code.

delete.description:
Cancel a login and answer with how it ended: `cancelled` when it was pending (a
code login stops polling Amazon; a browser login can no longer be completed), or
unchanged when it had already ended, so a code confirmed just before the cancel
reads `confirmed` and its account stays. 404 once the login has been forgotten.

get.description: How a login is going; 404 once it has been forgotten (a while after it ended).

post.description:
Step two of a browser login: the pasted address becomes the account.

404 for a login that is unknown, expired or already finished (start again), 400
for an address that carries no authorization code (the login stays open for the
right one), 409 when Amazon accepted but the login could not be stored - another
account holds it, the account has gone - which ends it, 502 when Amazon rejects
the code.

delete.description:
Remove an account, its library rows and its run history; files on disk stay.

With `deregister`, the device this login registered with Amazon is deregistered
first, so it does not linger on the account's device list. That is best effort:
a login that no longer works cannot deregister itself, and the account is
removed either way.

409 while the run in flight is on this account: its sync would leave rows behind
for an account that no longer exists, and its download a book on disk with no
row. An account the run has not reached yet is fine - the run reads each account
again at its turn and skips one that has gone.

get.description:
A page of the library. `q` matches the title, any author or any series; `title`,
`author`, `narrator` and `series` only those. Each is a contains match ignoring case and
the kind of apostrophe, and they combine.

post.description:
One action on many books: the ids selected, or everything the filters match.

The filters mean what they mean on `GET /api/books`, so "all 354 matching" acts
on the 354 the listing counted. Books a run is downloading, a retry of a
downloaded book and deleting the files of a book with none are skipped, each
with a reason; an unknown id is skipped as `not_found`. 404 for a filter on an
unknown account.

Queue every parked book Audible still reports consumable again.

For the day Audible refused every licence - a device registration it had
stopped accepting, say - rather than one title it has retired. A re-login
does this for the account by itself; this is the button for everything else.

get.description: The cover: the file once downloaded, Audible's URL before that.

post.description: Remove the files and unmonitor the book, so it stays deleted.
Remove the files and queue the book afresh, attempts reset.
Queue a failed or parked book again without touching any files it has.

get.description:
Authors whose name matches, from Audible's search suggestions. Audible knows
little more than the name; an author's books are a search by `author` name, as
the id here can differ from the one on their books.

schema.title: Response Catalog Authors Api Catalog Authors Get

get.description: One book of the catalogue, with its description. 404 when Audible has no such book.
The marketplace's categories, two levels deep; an id is a search's `category_id`.

schema.title: Response Catalog Categories Api Catalog Categories Get

get.description:
A page of a catalogue search by any of `keywords`, `title`, `author`, `narrator`
and `category_id` (at least one), in the account's marketplace.

Audible pages through only so many results (`reachable`) and repeats its last
page beyond that, so a page past them is a 422. Podcasts are left out, so a
page can hold fewer than `page_size`; `total` is Audible's.

The series called `name`, or whose title contains it, best first: the exact
matches, then by how many books of a keyword search for the name are in each.
Audible has no search by series, so this finds a series through its books;
`author` narrows the search. Each is then read with `GET /api/catalog/series/{asin}`.

schema.title: Response Find Series Api Catalog Series Get

get.description:
A series and every book Audible lists in it, in reading order. A position often
has several books, the editions of one title. 404 when the ASIN is not a series.
The newest log lines, oldest first, at or above `level`.

schema.title: Response List Marketplaces Api Marketplaces Get

get.description:
The books still to come, in the order a run takes them: each enabled account
that can log in, oldest purchase first, cut at `max_download` per account. A
plan rather than a promise (refusals, titles the sync restores, a run in flight;
see `library.next_run_queue`). `limit` is how many to list; `total` (planned)
and `waiting` count them all.
The token masked to its last four characters, and whether it is the env's or stored.

post.description:
Replace the token; the old one stops working at once. The new one is returned
this once and never logged. 409 when `AUDIBLE_SYNC_API_TOKEN` sets it.

Only from a signed-in web app (403 under the bearer token alone): a leaked token
must not be able to lock its owner's scripts out by rotating itself.
Send a sample event to `url`, or the configured webhook; 502 if it fails.

get.description: The numbers a dashboard opens with: per account and in total.

post.description: Start a run now; with `{"full": true}` one that re-reads every library in full.

get.description:
The books a run downloaded, failed and was refused, for the Activity screen.
`recorded` is false on a run from before the per-book records, which says so
rather than showing three empty lists.
FFmpeg, the library's disk, the key and the database, for the System card.

Every account's wishlist in one list, or one account's, as last read from Audible.

`sort` is `date_added` (newest first), `title` (A to Z) or `release_date` (newest
first); `order` turns it round. A book on two accounts' wishlists is two items.
Each is a catalogue book (marked in a library and on wishlists, as the catalogue's
are) with its `account_id` and `added_at`. `accounts` says when each account's
wishlist was last read, and the error of a read that failed since: its books are
then as of the last read that worked.

post.description:
Put a book on an account's wishlist, on Audible and here: `201` when it was not
on it, `200` when it was (Audible does not say; the table does). `409` for a
book the account owns, which does not go on its wishlist, or an account that
needs a sign-in; `404` for an ASIN Audible does not know or an unknown account.

Read the wishlists from Audible again now: one account's (`account_id`) or every
signed-in account's. A wishlist that cannot be read is not an error here: the
answer says so per account, as `GET /api/wishlist` does, and the others are read.

schema.title: Response Refresh Wishlists Api Wishlist Refresh Post

delete.description:
Take a book off an account's wishlist, on Audible and here. Audible is told even
when the book was not on it as last read, so one added on Audible since comes off
too; `404` then, since as far as the list knew it was not there.
